_what: Reference fixture: assert your preprocessing reproduces these before trusting any comparison.
_call_site: Call model.get_training_outputs(x), NOT model(x). forward() does NOT normalise; get_training_outputs applies _preprocess (x/127.5 - 1.0) first. Passing a [0,255] tensor straight to forward() feeds the model noise and it still returns plausible-looking scores. This failure survives a correct tensor_sha256, which is what makes it dangerous: a consumer hit it with a matching hash and top-5 scores of 0.025 against the 0.6119 below. Verify the SCORES, not just the hash.
_note: min_score_thresh MUST be pinned when loading; the detector filters at its own default inside NMS, and its weighted NMS blends everything above that threshold, so the output depends on it.

preprocess.letterbox: centred, black pad, aspect preserved (NOT stretched)
preprocess.order: RGB, CHW, float32, pixels in [0,255]; model divides by 127.5 and subtracts 1.0 internally
